body:
I think this needs an `os` option (like in custom modules) or an `allow_windows` option because some `sudo` implementations on Windows might cause UAC prompts if they don't support the `-n` flag.
A `binary`/`sudo_binary` option might also be a good idea in case people want to use this module with `doas`.

body: I'd prefer to keep the name as-is because I think it reflects the main functionality better. I would expect `superuser` or `elevated` to activate if the prompt was being run by a super user and not anything related to `sudo`.

I think this is missing the `-n` flag:
```suggestion
            .cmd("doas -n true", None)
```
Please mock `sudo -n true` for every test. Please don't need to mock other commands like `sudo -k` or `sudo -v` that will not be executed.

To fix the tests, you need to mock the expected value in every test and not only `None`. In this test, that would be the following:

```rust
Some(CommandOutput {
    stdout: "".to_owned(),
    stderr: "".to_owned(),
})
```
Can you add `allow_windows = true` to all the tests currently blocking windows and allow them to run there, to ensure `allow_windows = true` also works?

This test can run on Windows with the `allow_windows = true` change.

